mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS>5.0) are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 200.0) signals stable monetary conditions with favorable growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in the joint condition (FEDFUNDS<4.5 and CPIAUCSL<200.0) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (as indicated by high GDP growth), the market is overbought and vulnerable to correction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a weak labor market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high unemployment periods (UNRATE>5.0) are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
